question: What are the main benefits of 5G technology according to AT&T engineers?
transcript_excerpt: 5G supports a wide range of spectrum including millimeter wave frequencies from 24 to 300 gigahertz, providing speeds of 10 to 20 gigabit per second. It enables network slicing to provide specific services to public safety, healthcare, and industry without segments mixing. 5G also offers very low latency of about one to two milliseconds, enabling near real-time communication for video transmission and Internet of Things applications.

question: What is the difference between 4G and 5G cellular networks in terms of architecture?
transcript_excerpt: 4G collapsed voice and data into one complete IP network with no circuit switching, making it function more like the internet. 5G builds on this foundation with higher data rates and the ability to slice networks for specific purposes, whereas 3G used two separate networks—one for voice and one for data—which was costly for providers.

question: Is 5G radiation harmful to human health?
transcript_excerpt: The spectrum used for 5G is non-ionizing radiation, not ionizing radiation, so it does not provide any negative effects on users. While people may fear that propagating signals at high frequency generates ionized signals that could interfere with health, there are two types of radiation and 5G operates on the safe, non-ionizing type.

question: How did Usang Ekpe win the 2022 Dr. James Mitchell Legacy Award?
transcript_excerpt: Ekpe was nominated by his director at AT&T for the award and informed on October 26, 2021 that he won the Dr. James W. Mitchell Legacy Award. He believes he was nominated partly because when AT&T brought in international employees during a time when outsourcing was unpopular, he transferred his knowledge to a group of college students outside the country rather than viewing it as a threat to his job.

question: What is the history of cellular mobile phone technology from 1G to 5G?
transcript_excerpt: The first cellular phone call was made by Dr. Martin Cooper in 1973 in New York. 1G was introduced in 1981 and used analog technology with mechanical switches enabling only voice calls. 2G supported voice with limited data starting in 1992 with text messaging. 3G enabled voice and data but used two separate networks. 4G collapsed these into one IP network. 5G was introduced around 2018 with significantly higher data rates and new use cases.

question: Why did Usang Ekpe choose telecommunications engineering over petroleum engineering?
transcript_excerpt: At a career day in high school, a general manager from Nigeria's analog telecommunication company spoke about using mechanical analog switches to enable long-distance communication, which captivated Ekpe. He also recognized that electrical and electronics engineering is more dynamic than petroleum engineering, with new developments or improvements emerging every one to two years, and he prefers doing different things rather than repeating the same work.
